claims.explanation: HSP90 inhibition by NVP-AUY922 selectively kills cancer cells that depend on HSP90 client proteins for survival, particularly those with activated RTK/RAS/PI3K signaling and high HSP90 client expression. Tumors with BRAF, KRAS, NRAS, EGFR, MET, or PIK3CA mutations are more sensitive because their oncogenic drivers are HSP90 clients, while protective features include high baseline HSP70/HSPA1A expression and possibly TP53 wild-type status. The pattern suggests that sensitivity is driven by oncogene addiction to HSP90 clients rather than by a single lineage.

features.basis: BRAF is an HSP90 client; mutant BRAF is degraded upon HSP90 inhibition, and BRAF-mutant lines (e.g., BCPAP, 8305C, WM793) are among the most killed.
KRAS is an HSP90 client; KRAS-mutant lines (e.g., PK45H, SW1990, NCIH1792, SW1573, OV7) are enriched among sensitive lines.
NRAS is an HSP90 client; NRAS-mutant melanoma line IPC298 is among the most killed.
Mutant EGFR is an HSP90 client; EGFR-mutant lines (KYSE70, RL952) appear in the sensitive set.
MET is an HSP90 client; MET-mutant lines (HGC27, 8305C) are among the most killed.
PIK3CA-mutant lines (SNU840, KYSE70, HCC1954, HGC27, SW1573) are enriched in the sensitive group, consistent with PI3K/Akt dependence on HSP90.
High baseline HSP70 (HSPA1A) expression can compensate for HSP90 inhibition and is associated with resistance.
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, but TP53 wild-type status may enhance apoptosis; however, the pattern is weak.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/Akt signaling, which depends on HSP90; PTEN-mutant lines (WM793, SF126, SF295) are among the most killed.
NF1 loss activates RAS signaling; NF1-mutant lines (S117, COLO792) are among the most killed.
CDKN2A loss may increase dependence on HSP90 clients; CDKN2A-mutant lines (IPC298, 8305C) are among the most killed.
ARID1A mutation appears in both sensitive and resistant lines, but its presence in several resistant lines suggests possible protection.
